body_en:
When I was seventeen, I wrote you letter after letter, hoping to hold on to our awkward youth — to that foot of space between us where we met on the stairs, to the fierce sun of that summer.

But back then, a boy with his head in the clouds mistook love for a superpower.

And then, in the blink of an eye — the color of your pupils in my memory, the warmth of your skin, the particular smell of laundry detergent on your school uniform — all of it, along with the only tenderness we ever shared at sixteen or seventeen, was buried with the youth we left behind.
excerpt_en: At seventeen, I wrote her letter after letter, trying to hold on to our awkward youth — the foot of space between us on the stairs, the fierce summer sun. Then memory buried it all.
